Functional decline means losing the ability to carry out activities that were manageable before the emergency visit. Ask what the patient could do before the illness and what help will actually be available at home.
**None of these descriptions provides a reliable single exception. Needing help is clinically relevant regardless of the caregiver’s nationality.**

**A. Living alone** Establish who can check in, obtain prescriptions and help with daily activities. A person living alone may still have dependable support.

q: מה מהווה שינוי נורמלי בהזדקנות על הלב?

ירידה ב- pulse pressure
הופעה של mitral regurgitation
ירידה ב- aortic impedance
explanation:
**Mild mitral regurgitation** can be detected with advancing age as the valve apparatus degenerates. New symptomatic or more than mild regurgitation requires evaluation.

**A. Rightward ECG axis.** A gradual leftward shift is more typical.
**B. Lower pulse pressure.** Arterial stiffening usually widens pulse pressure.
**C. Mitral regurgitation.** Minor Doppler-detected leakage may accompany aging even without a major structural lesion.
**D. Lower aortic impedance.** Reduced arterial compliance tends to increase the load against which the ventricle ejects.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, Ch 73, pp. 1120–1121 and 1131.

explanation:
Pain and depression often coexist in cancer and can worsen disability together. Asking about both helps identify treatable suffering even when one symptom dominates the consultation.
**Greater cancer pain is associated with a higher burden of depressive symptoms.**

**A. More depression in men with cancer.** Male sex alone is not a reliable way to identify which oncology patients have depression.
**B. ACE inhibitors commonly cause depression.** Depression is not a characteristic common class effect. Review the timing of symptoms and other medical or psychosocial contributors.
**C. Hip-fracture depression usually persists long term.** An episode after fracture warrants follow-up. Its course varies with pain, recovery, disability and pre-existing depression.
**D. Association with pain severity.** More severe pain and greater depressive distress can occur together. The association does not tell which symptom came first in an individual.

q: מה המשמעות המשפטית של הסכמה מדעת בהקשר של חולה קשיש?
o: חתימה על טופס מספיקה גם בלי הסבר על הסיכונים והחלופות
מתן מידע מלא על הטיפול, סיכונים, חלופות, ווידוא הבנה — ללא קשר לגיל
הסכמת בן משפחה מחליפה את הסכמתו של המטופל המבוגר גם כאשר הוא מבין ומחליט
אפשר לצמצם את המידע הנמסר למטופל לפי גילו, בלי להתאים את ההסבר להבנתו
explanation:
ההסבר למטופל מבוגר צריך להיות מובן ונגיש. בודקים שהוא מבין את התועלת, הסיכונים והחלופות ושהבחירה שלו. **מתן מידע מלא על הטיפול, סיכונים, חלופות, ווידוא הבנה — ללא קשר לגיל**.

**א. חתימה על טופס מספיקה גם בלי הסבר על הסיכונים והחלופות.** טופס חתום אינו משלים מידע שחסר.
**ב. מתן מידע מלא על הטיפול, סיכונים, חלופות, ווידוא הבנה — ללא קשר לגיל.** כך מתאפשרת בחירה חופשית על בסיס מידע רפואי.
**ג. הסכמת בן משפחה מחליפה את הסכמתו של המטופל המבוגר גם כאשר הוא מבין ומחליט.** בני המשפחה אינם מחליפים מטופל כשיר.
**ד. אפשר לצמצם את המידע הנמסר למטופל לפי גילו, בלי להתאים את ההסבר להבנתו.** גיל כשלעצמו אינו מצדיק לצמצם את ההסבר.

q: מי רשאי לפנות לוועדה המוסדית לפי חוק החולה הנוטה למות?
o: מנהל המוסד או רופא שמינה רשאים לפנות; המטופל ונציגיו נדרשים לקבל קודם את אישור הנהלת המוסד שבו הוא מטופל
המטופל או מי מטעמו, מיופה כוחו, קרוב או אפוטרופוס ללא־כשיר, מטפל במוסד, רופאו האישי או עובד סוציאלי
בן משפחה מכל דרגת קרבה או עובד מנהלה במוסד רשאים לפנות גם ללא קשר טיפולי או מעמד לפי החוק
הפנייה נעשית באמצעות בית המשפט לאחר בקשה של המשפחה; צוות הטיפול אינו פונה ישירות לוועדה
explanation:
הוועדה המוסדית לפי חוק החולה הנוטה למות מוסמכת לברר מחלוקות המנויות בחוק. אפשר לפנות אליה ישירות מתוך מעגל החולה והטיפול. **המטופל או מי מטעמו, מיופה כוחו, קרוב או אפוטרופוס ללא־כשיר, מטפל במוסד, רופאו האישי או עובד סוציאלי**.

**א. מנהל המוסד או רופא שמינה רשאים לפנות; המטופל ונציגיו נדרשים לקבל קודם את אישור הנהלת המוסד שבו הוא מטופל.** אין למנהל בלעדיות על הפנייה.
**ב. המטופל או מי מטעמו, מיופה כוחו, קרוב או אפוטרופוס ללא־כשיר, מטפל במוסד, רופאו האישי או עובד סוציאלי.** הרשימה כוללת את החולה ונציגיו ואת המטפלים ובעלי התפקיד הרלוונטיים לפי החוק.
**ג. בן משפחה מכל דרגת קרבה או עובד מנהלה במוסד רשאים לפנות גם ללא קשר טיפולי או מעמד לפי החוק.** עצם קשר משפחתי רחוק או תפקיד מינהלי אינו מקנה זכות ללא תנאי.
**ד. הפנייה נעשית באמצעות בית המשפט לאחר בקשה של המשפחה; צוות הטיפול אינו פונה ישירות לוועדה.** בית משפט אינו תחנת חובה לפני דיון בוועדה.

אסמכתא · חוק החולה הנוטה למות, סעיף 46(א), עמ׳ 23–24.

q: A 76-year-old man with HFpEF receives a diuretic for congestion. After excessive diuresis he develops fatigue, low blood pressure, and worsening prerenal azotemia. Which mechanism explains this risk?
o: Increased ventricular diastolic volume with increased congestion
Reduced ventricular diastolic volume with reduced cardiac output
Increased ventricular contractility with increased stroke volume
Prolonged ventricular filling time with increased cardiac output
explanation:
In HFpEF the stiff ventricle has limited ability to increase filling. **Excessive diuresis reduces end-diastolic volume and forward output**, explaining both hypotension and prerenal azotemia.

**A. Increased filling volume** That would favor rising filling pressure and recurrent congestion, the opposite of the immediate change.
**B. Reduced filling and output** Removing too much preload reduces stroke volume. At a similar heart rate, cardiac output falls.
**C. Increased contractility** A diuretic has no direct positive inotropic action to explain this sequence.
**D. Longer filling time** Filling time depends chiefly on heart rate and rhythm. The acute problem here is insufficient returning blood.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1186.

q: An 80-year-old man with lower urinary tract symptoms and postural dizziness takes terazosin. Why might a selective alpha blocker such as tamsulosin be considered?
o: Less dizziness, with less reduction in urinary symptoms
More dizziness, with similar reduction in urinary symptoms
Less dizziness, with similar reduction in urinary symptoms
More dizziness, with greater reduction in urinary symptoms
explanation:
Terazosin and tamsulosin both reduce smooth muscle tone at the bladder outlet. **Tamsulosin generally causes less dizziness while providing similar improvement in urinary symptoms.**

**A. Less dizziness and less urinary relief** — The safety advantage is plausible, but trials did not show a significant loss of urinary symptom benefit with the more selective agent.
**B. More dizziness with similar relief** — The efficacy comparison is reasonable. The expected direction of the postural adverse effect is reversed.
**C. Less dizziness with similar relief** — Greater selectivity for prostatic receptors limits the blood-pressure effect. Monitor for ongoing dizziness because it can still occur.
**D. More dizziness and greater relief** — Trials did not show superior symptom reduction with tamsulosin, and terazosin generally has more pronounced blood-pressure effects.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 564, 566, Table 38-6 and alpha-adrenergic blockers.

q: An older man with dementia and parkinsonism develops rigidity, fever and confusion after a dopamine-blocking drug is added. He also takes a bladder antimuscarinic and has dry skin. Which mechanisms can contribute to this rise in body temperature?
o: Neuroleptic-induced hyperthermia and impaired sweat production.
Serotonin toxicity from dopamine blockade and loss of salt in sweat.
Thyroid hormone excess and increased cutaneous heat transfer.
Infectious fever and increased evaporative cooling from skin.
explanation:
Fever with rigidity and confusion after a medication change raises concern for a drug-related emergency. **Neuroleptics can cause hyperthermia in neuroleptic malignant syndrome, and anticholinergics reduce sweating**.

**A. Neuroleptic-induced hyperthermia and impaired sweat production** — Neuroleptic malignant syndrome can cause fever, rigidity and confusion. Antimuscarinic drugs limit evaporative heat loss by reducing sweating.
**B. Serotonin toxicity from dopamine blockade and loss of salt in sweat** — Dopamine blockade is associated with neuroleptic malignant syndrome. Cholinergic sweat production is inhibited by antimuscarinic drugs.
**C. Thyroid hormone excess and increased cutaneous heat transfer** — Neither of these drug effects is mediated by thyroid hormone. Impaired heat loss can worsen hyperthermia.
**D. Infectious fever and increased evaporative cooling from skin** — Infection should be evaluated clinically, but it does not explain the additive medication effects on thermoregulation.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 585.
ref: Hazzard Ch 39 — SYSTEMS PHYSIOLOGY OF AGING AND SELECTED DISORDERS OF HOMEOSTASIS

q: What is the mechanism of photodynamic therapy for actinic keratoses according to Hazzard?
o: Destroying tissue through freezing of the lesion with liquid nitrogen
Triggering an immune response through activation of toll-like receptor 7
Blocking cellular DNA synthesis through inhibition of the enzyme thymidylate synthetase
Applying a photosensitizing agent and activating it with light
explanation:
Photodynamic therapy treats selected actinic keratoses by generating local injury when light activates a sensitizer. **Apply the photosensitizing agent and illuminate the treated area**.

**A. Freeze with nitrogen.** Cryotherapy causes ice-mediated tissue destruction.
**B. Activate toll-like receptor 7.** This is imiquimod's immunologic mechanism.
**C. Inhibit thymidylate synthase.** Fluorouracil interferes with DNA synthesis through this mechanism.
**D. Sensitizer plus light.** Both application of the agent and subsequent light exposure are needed for the local effect.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1461, 1460.

. Sensitizer plus light.** Both application of the agent and subsequent light exposure are needed for the local effect.

q: A 77-year-old woman with AML in remission after venetoclax/azacitidine, diabetes, and depression has stopped driving and cooking and sleeps much of the day. Her MMSE is 26/30. She takes prophylactic acyclovir, metformin, and long-standing sertraline 100 mg daily. Examination shows psychomotor slowing, and her CBC is normal. If hypothyroidism is being evaluated as a possible contributor, which initial assessment does Hazzard recommend?
o: Measure antithyroid antibodies as the initial diagnostic assessment
Measure serum TSH as the initial diagnostic assessment
Measure serum T3 as the initial diagnostic assessment
Diagnose hypothyroidism from the pattern of cognitive and behavioral symptoms
explanation:
Psychomotor slowing and loss of function can accompany hypothyroidism but have many causes. **Measure serum TSH first when evaluating possible primary hypothyroidism.**

**A. Antithyroid antibodies** Antibodies can reflect autoimmunity. They do not tell whether the gland currently provides sufficient hormone.
**B. Serum TSH** The pituitary increases TSH when a failing thyroid needs more stimulation. Free T4 clarifies an abnormal TSH and should also be checked if central disease is suspected.
**C. Serum T3** T3 is unhelpful for diagnosing hypothyroidism and can fall during unrelated illness.
**D. Diagnose from symptoms** Depression, systemic disease and medication effects can produce similar functional changes. Confirm thyroid status biochemically.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1551–1552, Hypothyroidism.

. Serum T3** T3 is unhelpful for diagnosing hypothyroidism and can fall during unrelated illness.

q: בן 75, לוקה בדמנציה מתקדמת, אובחן עם Aortic Stenosis במסגרת בירור כאבים בחזה. באקו לב שטח מסתם 0.6 cm2, מפל לחצים 50 mmHg, מהירות זרימה 5 m/s. מה הגישה הטיפולית הנכונה למטופל?
o: Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement (SAVR)
Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement (TAVR)
טיפול פליאטיבי לצורך הקלת התסמינים
בהעדר קריטריונים להתערבות לבצע בדיקה חוזרת בעוד שנה
explanation:
Chest pain with a valve area of 0.6 cm², mean gradient of 50 mm Hg and velocity of 5 m/s indicates severe symptomatic aortic stenosis. Treatment choice also depends on whether intervention can deliver survival or function the patient would value.
**In the vignette, advanced dementia favors a palliative plan directed at symptom relief.**

**A. Surgical replacement.** Open surgery carries the greatest recovery burden. Its benefit is uncertain when advanced dementia substantially limits the prospect of meaningful functional recovery.
**B. Transcatheter replacement.** A less invasive route still carries procedural risks. Severe dementia remains relevant even when transfemoral access is technically possible.
**C. Palliative symptom control.** Discuss goals with the patient as able and their surrogate. Treat distressing symptoms when the burden of valve intervention is unlikely to yield a meaningful benefit.
**D. Repeat echocardiography in a year.** The symptoms and measurements already indicate severe disease. This patient needs a goals-of-care and treatment decision now.

explanation:
Ultrasound helps identify thyroid nodules that warrant cytology. **Calcification is the relevant choice when it represents suspicious microcalcifications within a nodule.**

**A. Female sex** Nodules are common in women, but a nodule carries a higher malignancy risk in men.
**B. Multiple nodules** Multiplicity alone does not raise the patient's risk above that with a solitary nodule. Assess each nodule's appearance.
**C. Calcifications** Intranodular microcalcifications are a high-risk ultrasound feature, alongside irregular margins and a taller-than-wide shape. The broad word “calcifications” needs this qualification.
**D. Palpable nodule** For lesions of the same size, palpability alone does not distinguish malignant from benign nodules.

q: בן 75 אחרי שבר בצוואר הירך עם כאב נוירופטי ומצב רוח ירוד. ברקע מטופל ב- LEVETIRACETAM (KEPRRA) על רקע מחלה פרכוסית. סובל מזיהום בפצע הניתוחי. איזה מהתרופות הבאות לא תעלה את הסיכון לפרכוסים?
o: TRAMADOL (TRAMADEX)
CIPROFLOXACIN (CIPRO)
BUPROPION (WELLBUTRIN)
PREGABALIN (LYRICA)
explanation:
Drugs that lower the seizure threshold can provoke breakthrough seizures despite antiseizure treatment. For this man taking levetiracetam, **pregabalin** treats neuropathic pain and is also used as an adjunct for focal seizures.

**A. Tramadol.** This analgesic can provoke seizures even at therapeutic doses. A history of epilepsy increases concern.
**B. Ciprofloxacin.** This fluoroquinolone can cause central nervous system excitation and seizures. Impaired renal clearance can increase exposure.
**C. Bupropion.** Its dose-related seizure risk makes it contraindicated in someone with an established seizure disorder, despite the depressive symptoms.
**D. Pregabalin.** It binds the alpha-2-delta subunit of voltage-gated calcium channels and reduces excitatory neurotransmitter release. Adjust for kidney function and watch for dizziness during hip-fracture recovery.

Reference · Harrison 21e, p. 3311, Table 425-5, and Hazzard 8e, pp. 1063–1064.

explanation:
Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) produces multifocal bile-duct strictures. **MR cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) can show characteristic stricturing and beading** in large-duct PSC.

**A. Hepatitis C serology because 80 percent develop cirrhosis.** Testing for HCV is reasonable, but the option confuses persistence of infection with the smaller proportion progressing to cirrhosis.
**B. AMA positive in only 20 to 40 percent of PBC.** Antimitochondrial antibodies are present in most patients with primary biliary cholangitis.
**C. MRCP for PSC.** The duct pattern can support diagnosis without using invasive cholangiography as the initial study.
**D. Echocardiography diagnoses cardiac cirrhosis.** Echo can show the cardiac disorder causing hepatic congestion. It does not by itself diagnose established cirrhosis.
